## TL;DR
When a release is cut, any project with an email provider configured can email its team the release notes, with a Releases-page card for status, preview, Resend and the bell. This round closes the review-3 verdict: the earlier handoff already fixed the four named bugs, and I then closed the two remaining edge cases — a resend after a restart can no longer announce a version GitHub has not published, and the "Set up email" hint now points at the raw TOML the provider actually lives in rather than a Settings tab with no email control.

## Work and rationale
`release-email.ts` renders and sends one message per recipient through the configured provider (`server/email.ts`, the single outbound mail path), records each accepted address before the next send, and records the outcome per version in a gitignored `release-emails.json`. The earlier commit `3d1564aee` had already fixed the review-3 bugs: the Releases view reloads the email state in `pollRun`'s success branch (`Promise.all([load(), loadDistribution(), loadReleaseEmail()])`), the accepted-recipient list is caller-owned and pushed onto as each address is accepted so the catch records every one, `getReleaseEmailRecord` surfaces an orphaned `pending` record to the bell, and the docs were reworded to per-recipient at-most-once with the provider-200-to-local-write window.

This round addresses the review-3 edge cases that were left open.

**Resend after a restart skipped the publish gate.** An orphaned `pending` record reads as `failed`, so Resend would send at once — possibly before GitHub has the release. `resendReleaseEmail` now does one live `probeRelease` when `when === "published"` and `[release].repository` is set. A `not-yet` or `http-error` answer refuses the send with a reason the UI shows ("GitHub does not have vX published yet … Send once it is, or set when = tagged"); `published` proceeds; `unreachable` proceeds too, matching the automatic path's documented no-network fallback to the tag. This is deliberately one probe, not the hour-long wait — a person is clicking, so the right answer is "not yet, try again" rather than holding a button for an hour.

**The "Set up email" link led nowhere useful.** It pointed at `/settings?tab=security`, but `auth.emailProvider.*` has no Settings control at all — it is raw TOML (it is not in `getConfigSchema()`, and neither `AuthSettingsPanel.vue` nor the security tab mentions the provider). The hint now names `[auth.emailProvider]` and `REPOOS_RESEND_API_KEY` and links to `/settings?tab=toml`, the raw-TOML editor, where the value is actually set. I avoided inventing an in-app `/docs/native-auth` route that would 404 and instead kept the pointer to the file the person must edit.

**Tests.** Four new `resendReleaseEmail` cases with a fake fetch: refuse when GitHub 404s, send when GitHub serves the release, fall back at the tag when GitHub is unreachable, and refuse on an HTTP error status (rate limit) rather than sending early. The existing restart test already supplies a published GitHub response, so it exercises the new gate too. `docs/releases.md` and `user-docs/configuration.md` now state the resend publish check, and `docs/releases.md`'s known-gaps list no longer claims Resend "sends at once instead" — it re-probes, then sends.

## Approaches tried
For the no-network resend case I first considered reusing the whole `waitForPublishedRelease` loop, but rejected it: the loop's one-hour timeout is right for the detached automatic path and wrong for a button a human just pressed. One `probeRelease` call gives the same "is it downloadable yet?" answer without freezing the UI. For the setup link I first wrote a two-link hint pointing at a `/docs/native-auth` page, then dropped it after confirming the UI router has no docs route — a dead link is worse than no link.

## Challenges and blockers
The prior handoff failed with "server-side finalization timed out (deadline exceeded)", and the last stored check run showed `tests` and `ui-smoke` failing. Both reproduce as flakes only: `ai-role-tracking.test.ts` and `handoff-unification.test.ts` pass in isolation, `scripts/ui-smoke.mjs` passes in isolation, and the scoped `repoos check` this round is fully green (the suite ran on the remote runner). The failures carry the shape of the known memory-pressure flake the repo documents, not a branch regression — nothing in this diff touches session recording, handoff finalization or first-paint. I left two pre-existing race fixes in `serve-reaper.test.ts` and `agent-process-group.test.ts` (fixed sleeps replaced with event waits) on the branch: the review suggested splitting them out, but I cannot write commits from the runner sandbox, and reverting them would reintroduce the very flakiness that made this gate unstable.

One review edge case I deliberately left as-is: `[release.email] enabled` with `[release] enabled` unset still saves from Settings, with only a load-time warning from `parseReleaseEmailConfig`. The recipe already warns, the field description states the requirement, and no release can be cut while `[release]` is off — so nothing is ever sent. Adding cross-field save validation is a larger UI change than this edge warrants; the reviewer flagged it as informational across two passes.

## Key learnings
A derived-on-read status (`pending` → `failed` after a restart) is also a behaviour change: any action the UI offers for `failed` must hold under the original `when` gate, or the recovery path silently weakens the guarantee the happy path enforces. And when a hint says "set up X", verify X has a real control on the page it links to — here the email provider only ever lived in `repoos.toml`, so the honest link was the file, not a Settings tab.
